subject: Embedding external functions to process temperature data

messages.author: 46551ba1f83aaf38
messages.subject: Embedding external functions to process temperature data
parts:
Hello everybody, 

I would like to embed an external function for non-wear detection that uses also temperature data. In the docs I saw that the external function is expected to take as input a three-column matrix with the acceleration data. Is there a way to have as input the temperature data as well (i.e., a four-column matrix)?

Thanks a lot, 
Marcello

messages.author: b9400d58a0bfce63
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Embedding external functions to process temperature data
parts:
Hi Marcello,

As far as I know (but could be wrong of course), there is not a pre-packaged way to do this with the external function parameter settings.However, you could easily make a minor customization to allow this.

The good news is that the external function (applyExtFunction.R is the relevant script) is already provided initially with data that includes the temperature data for your device. However, basically the first operation performed removes everything except for the acceleration columns. You can see that line of code here: https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/blob/40869c8754bb0c06913b57c1709c9c1197c3ccbe/R/applyExtFunction.R#L2

So my approach would be to add a logical parameter to `applyExtFunction` called something like "include.temp". Then modify the applyExtFunction to include a 4th column in the the data matrix for temperature if include.temp == T. Note that to do this you also have to modify the function "check_myfun.R" because it is programmed to search for unexpected parameters and throw an error if there's an issue.

These minor modifications could be incorporated into GGIR, but if I had to guess there is probably a reason that this is a bad idea (though unless the include.temp parameter is set, it wouldn't break anything...).

In case it's helpful I included two modified script files that overwrite the GGIR package functions making the suggested changes. Hope this helps,

Tom

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Embedding external functions to process temperature data
parts:
Hi Marcello,

As Tom clarified, using of temperature data in the external function is not possible at the moment, unless you dive into the code and make your own edits like Tom did.

I designed the external function embedding option to aid deriving additional signal features (metrics), which are then treated by the rest of GGIR as any of the following:
  • scalar similar to ENMO, MAD, counts, etc.
  • event such as steps.
  • character which we used as indicator of sleep
Nonwear detection is not an option at the moment. So, even if your calculation would reflect an improved non-wear classification then GGIR will not be able to use it at the moment.

It may be easier to explore this as a direct addition to GGIR (via pull request) rather than as external function.

Let me know if you want to develop this.

Best wishes,

Vincent
